item.title: Java Swing: Implementing Interactive Line Drawing with Mouse and Key Bindings
item.description:
“Java Swing: Implementing Interactive Line Drawing with Mouse and Key Bindings”

Achieving fluid, interactive graphics in Java Swing generally involves extending JPanel and overriding paintComponent(Graphics g) to handle rendering, coupled with event listeners for user input. The primary difficulty lies in ensuring that drawing operations persist across window resizing or focus changes, which necessitates drawing within the paintComponent method rather than directly from event handlers using getGraphics().

Preferred Approach: Persistent Drawing in paintComponent with Mouse Events

A robust solution involves tracking the start point ($\text{p1}$) and end point ($\text{p2}$) of the line within the panel’s state. Mouse events are used to update these points, triggering a repaint request.
